ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #20
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

2. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. run
   C. blue
   D. quickly

3. When practising Pronunciation and Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Listening.

4. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. No full stops
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

5. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. goes
   C. going
   D. went

6. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.

7. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

8. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.

9. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.

10. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.

11. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only an action
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

12. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 13.4.1 Mechanics of writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

2. B — run

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Listening.

4. C — One main idea with supporting sentences

5. D — went

6. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes.

7. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

8. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.

9. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Guided Writing.

10. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.

11. D — A person, place, thing, or idea

12. B — Where is the library?

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 13.4.1 Mechanics of writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
